notes:
Shape. 14 domains and 160 leaves; the brief asked for about 12 and 120 to 160. AI and agent tooling, and wallets and retail support, each kept their own domain because the brief names them as must-cover topics and they share no canonical source with their neighbours. 36 leaves (22.5%) are weight 3. Volatility: 43 stable, 81 scheduled, 36 live.

Method. Built from the supply side only: developers.stellar.org/llms.txt and its three sub-indexes (Build, Data, Platforms), the stellar-protocol SEP and CAP index READMEs, the docs Software Versions page, the stellar GitHub organization listing, the stellar.org sitemap, the SCF handbook repository tree, and Raven's own search plus enumeration calls against Scout and Lumenloop. eval/qa and eval/corpus were not read. Weights are my judgment from supply-side signals (how much documentation, tooling, and funding a topic has, and whether a wrong answer loses funds or breaks a build); the demand-side map should override them where real question volume disagrees.

Raven reach. 66 leaves were spot-checked (all 36 weight-3 leaves first, then the topics the brief suspected of having no good source): 42 yes, 21 partial, 3 no. The three 'no' leaves are wallets.lost-funds-memos, wallets.unsolicited-assets, and org.xlm-markets-products. Each check was one search on the leaf question and one operation call; ravenCheck records what came back. A 'partial' means on-topic rows returned but the specific answer was not in them. These are reach observations for the gap ledger, not statements of fact.

Things the reconciler should know.
- Naming conflict, Freighter and Varial. The docs wallet guide and Scout say Freighter was renamed Varial (Scout: 'renamed 2026-10-29'). The stellar/freighter repositories, the Software Versions table, and Scout's partner list still say Freighter.
- stellar.org/community says 'Stellar launched independently in 2015'; SDF's 'A Look Back at Stellar's First Year' post is dated 2015-07-31, which implies a 2014 start. Treat the launch year as disputed wording, not a single fact.
- stellar.org/foundation/roadmap was still titled '2025 SDF Product Roadmap' on 2026-11-14, while the strategy page is dated 2026.
- The docs APIs overview says Horizon 'is nearing end-of-life'; any Horizon leaf should be read with that status.
- The Tier 1 page has requirements and costs but no roster; the current Tier 1 set is not in any source Raven reaches.
- network.protocol-versions and tooling.version-compat depend on one very long page (about 150k characters) that search surfaces at its oldest section.
- Scout's people index quotes stellar.org/foundation/team as observed on 2026-07-19.
- Lumenloop's proposals collection (202 rows) contains test rows, including one whose title is an HTML injection string. It is untrusted data and was not acted on.
- Application-level exploits (security.defi-exploits) have no SDF or docs page; the sources are third-party write-ups and Lumenloop articles.
- 37 canonicalSources entries are marked unverified: the URL was listed in the stellar.org sitemap or a search result but the page was not opened.

Left out, and why.
- XLM price forecasts, trading advice, and tax treatment: no Stellar source, and jurisdiction-specific.
- Per-endpoint reference detail (Horizon resource objects, Anchor Platform and Disbursement Platform endpoints, Hubble table dictionaries): details inside a leaf, not leaves.
- SEPs and CAPs not attached to a leaf, including rejected and draft CAPs (SPEEDEX CAP-0044 and CAP-0045, CAP-0072, CAP-0089, CAP-0090), abandoned SEPs (3, 13, 26), and low-traffic SEPs (2 federation, 11 txrep, 14, 18, 33 identicons, 35, 37, 59, 60): covered only through standards.sep-process and network.cap-process.
- Retired or historical products (Starlight payment channels, Starbridge, the Lightning roadmap, inflation pool voting, early airdrops): history only, inside org.history-origins and org.xlm-supply.

They sit under org.project-directory, funding.hackathons, and funding.meridian.
- Marketing framings that repeat a payments leaf: PayFi, exchange and FX, treasury management, and enterprise applications pages on stellar.org.
- Sustainability and energy use, brand policy, careers, and code of conduct.
- Minor developer tools: online IDE, Jupyter notebooks, asset sandbox, Quickstart cloud deployment pages, and CLI plugins.
